about.title: Mission Viejo Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A blender that shatters mid-cycle, a space heater that ignites, a child's car seat whose latch gives way — defective products reach Mission Viejo households the same way they reach the rest of Orange County: through ordinary shopping trips and online orders. When one of them hurts someone, California law does not ask the injured person to prove the manufacturer was careless. Under strict liability, the question is whether the product had a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or an inadequate warning, and whether that defect caused the harm. Defects also show up on the road. Among the 210 injury collisions recorded in Mission Viejo in 2025, some crashes on I-5 or Marguerite Parkway may trace back to a failed component rather than a driver's mistake, and that possibility deserves a look. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who takes product cases on contingency — no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Mission Viejo Residents Turn to LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict liability works in your favor
items.desc: In California you generally do not have to show the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective in design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. The attorney we connect you with knows how to frame a claim around that standard.

items.title: Guidance on preserving the evidence
items.desc: The product itself is usually the heart of the case, so it should not be thrown away, repaired, or returned. Early advice on keeping the item, packaging, receipts, and photos can protect a claim before it is ever filed.

items.title: Every link in the supply chain is examined
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers may all share responsibility under California law. An independent attorney can identify each party that placed the product in your hands, which matters when one company is out of state or out of business.

items.question: My airbag did not deploy in a crash on Alicia Parkway. Could that be a product liability claim?
items.answer: It might be. If a safety system failed to perform as designed, the collision may involve both a driver claim and a defect claim against the vehicle or component maker. Keep the car from being scrapped or repaired until an attorney has had a chance to evaluate it, since the physical evidence is essential. A free connection through LawProactive is a simple first step.

items.question: I bought the product online, not from a store in Mission Viejo. Does that matter?
items.answer: Generally, no. California's strict liability rules focus on the product's defect and the parties in its chain of distribution, not on where the checkout happened. Save your order confirmation, shipping records, and any listing screenshots, because they help establish who sold and supplied the item.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a product liability claim in California?
items.answer: Most personal injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the injury, though certain facts can shift that window. Because deadlines vary and evidence can disappear quickly, it is wise to speak with an attorney early. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney for free so you can learn where your timeline stands.
